examples.en: Curly perms are back in fashion these days.

examples.ko: 제 머리는 비가 오면 더 곱슬곱슬해져요.
examples.en: My hair gets curlier when it rains.
The baby's hair is curly and so cute.
After getting a curly perm, I look softer.
This puppy has curly fur.
I went to the salon to straighten my curly hair.

explain: 머리카락이나 강아지 털처럼 가늘게 말려 있는 것에 써요. 반대로 곧은 머리는 '생머리'라고 해요. 활용은 '곱슬곱슬해요', '곱슬곱슬한'이에요.
explain_en: It is used for things that curl finely, like hair or a dog's fur. Straight hair is called '생머리'. It conjugates as '곱슬곱슬해요' and '곱슬곱슬한'.

examples.en: I played all summer, so my face became tanned.
My younger sibling has dark skin and looks healthy.
Her white teeth look pretty against her dark skin.
My arms are dark from being in the sun.
Her skin is dark, but her face is clear and pretty.
Children with deeply tanned skin are playing on the beach.

explain: 주로 사람의 피부가 약간 검은 모습을 말해요. '가무잡잡하다'와 비슷한 말이고, '거무스름하다'보다 피부에 쓸 때가 더 많아요. 칭찬이 될 때도 있지만 상대에 따라 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It mainly describes skin that is somewhat dark. It is similar to '가무잡잡하다', and compared with '거무스름하다' it is more often used for skin. It can sound like a compliment, but use it carefully depending on the person.

examples.ko: 이 몸뚱이로는 무거운 짐을 못 들겠어요.
examples.en: With this body of mine, I can't carry heavy loads.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 누워 있었더니 몸뚱이가 무거워요.
examples.en: I lay around all day, and my body feels heavy.

examples.ko: 뱀은 머리는 작은데 몸뚱이는 아주 길어요.
examples.en: A snake has a small head but a very long body.

examples.ko: 눈사람은 큰 몸뚱이에 작은 얼굴을 달았어요.
examples.en: The snowman has a big body with a small face.

examples.ko: 이 몸뚱이 하나 믿고 여기까지 왔어요.
examples.en: I got this far trusting just this one body of mine.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 낡은 몸뚱이를 이끌고 시장에 가세요.
examples.en: My grandfather drags his worn-out body to the market.

explain: '몸'보다 거칠고 가벼운 느낌이어서 다른 사람 몸에는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요. '이 몸뚱이'처럼 자기 몸을 낮추거나 힘들다고 말할 때, 동물이나 물건의 몸통을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It is rougher and less polite than 몸, so avoid using it for another person's body. You use it for your own body when you are being self-deprecating or tired, as in 이 몸뚱이, and for the trunk of an animal or object.

dis.h: blunt, rough word; whole body or torso

p.n: The swap is neutral; the original is blunt and stresses the bulk of the body.

examples.en: Grandfather's hair has turned white, but he is very healthy.
A white-haired grandmother got on the bus.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 백발로 염색하고 새 영화에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actor dyed his hair white and appeared in the new movie.
He had white hair and wore glasses.
I dyed my hair to hide the gray.
The professor with a head of white hair began the lecture.

explain: 머리 전체가 하얗게 센 모습은 '백발'이라고 해요. 몇 가닥만 센 것은 '흰머리'라고 하고, 젊은 나이에 센 머리카락은 '새치'라고 따로 불러요. 보통 나이 드신 분의 모습을 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: 백발 is a whole head of white hair. A few white strands are 흰머리, and gray hairs that appear at a young age are called 새치. It is mostly used when describing older people.

examples.en: A velvet sofa feels very soft to the touch.

examples.ko: 그녀는 파란 벨벳 드레스를 입고 나왔어요.
examples.en: She came out wearing a blue velvet dress.

examples.ko: 극장 의자는 빨간 벨벳으로 덮여 있어요.
examples.en: The theater seats are covered in red velvet.
Velvet dresses are popular in winter.

examples.ko: 이 상자 안은 검은 벨벳으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The inside of this box is made of black velvet.
Thanks to the velvet curtains, the room is dark.

explain: 벨벳은 겉이 보들보들하고 부드러운 천이에요. 같은 천을 '비로드'라고도 불러요. '벨벳 케이크'처럼 음식 이름에도 붙어요.
explain_en: 벨벳 is a fabric with a soft, plush surface. The same fabric is also called 비로드. It also appears in food names, as in 벨벳 케이크 (red velvet cake).

en: bulging; protrudingly in a rounded way

examples.en: His belly is sticking out round.

examples.ko: 다람쥐가 입에 먹이를 넣어 볼을 볼록 부풀렸어요.
examples.en: The squirrel stuffed food in its mouth and puffed out its cheeks.
The balloon swelled up round.
Your pocket is bulging out.

examples.ko: 이불 속에서 고양이 등이 볼록 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A cat's back rose up in a round bump under the blanket.

examples.ko: 아이가 가방을 볼록 채워서 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child went to school with a bulging bag.

explain: 볼록은 둥글게 살짝 튀어나온 모양에 써요. 더 크고 많이 튀어나오면 '불룩'을 쓰는데 느낌이 더 커요. 반대로 안쪽으로 들어간 모양은 '오목'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 볼록 describes a slight, round bulge. For something bigger and more swollen, Koreans use '불룩', which feels stronger. The opposite, a dent going inward, is '오목'.

examples.en: I had an X-ray exam at the hospital.

examples.ko: 엑스선으로 찍으면 뼈 상태를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: With an X-ray, you can see the condition of the bones.

examples.ko: 엑스선은 눈에 보이지 않지만 몸을 통과해요.
examples.en: X-rays are invisible, but they pass through the body.
At the airport, you put your bag through an X-ray machine.

examples.ko: 엑스선 사진을 보니 다행히 부러지지 않았대요.
examples.en: The X-ray picture shows that, luckily, it isn't broken.
At the dentist, they took an X-ray and checked for cavities.

explain: 병원에서는 '엑스레이'라는 말을 더 많이 써요. 사진은 '엑스레이 사진', 찍는 것은 '엑스레이를 찍다'라고 해요. '엑스선'은 그 빛(전자기파)의 이름이라 설명문이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: At hospitals people more often say '엑스레이'. The image is called '엑스레이 사진' and taking one is '엑스레이를 찍다'. '엑스선' is the name of the ray itself, so it appears more in explanations and the news.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자면 병에 대한 저항력이 떨어져요.
examples.en: If you can't sleep, your resistance to illness drops.
Exercise is important to build up resistance.
Resistance gets weaker as you get older.
Does taking vitamins help your resistance?

examples.ko: 몸의 저항력 덕분에 독감에도 가볍게 지나갔어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my body's resistance, even the flu passed lightly.
I chose a plant that resists the cold well.

explain: 병이나 추위, 스트레스 같은 나쁜 영향에 맞서 버티는 힘이에요. 몸의 병뿐 아니라 추위나 충격에 버티는 힘에도 써요. 병에 대해서는 '면역력'이라고 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the strength to withstand bad influences such as illness, cold or stress. It is used not just for disease but also for resisting cold or shock. For illness, people more often say '면역력'.

examples.en: My face burned with embarrassment.

examples.ko: 매운 고추를 씹자 입안이 화끈 불붙은 것 같았어요.
examples.en: When I bit into a hot pepper, my mouth felt like it was on fire.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물이 닿자 손이 화끈 아팠어요.
examples.en: When hot water touched it, my hand stung hotly.
My forehead feels burning hot, maybe from a cold.

examples.ko: 민망한 말을 듣고 귀까지 화끈 뜨거워졌어요.
examples.en: After hearing that embarrassing remark, even my ears flushed hot.
I put a heat pack on in midwinter, and my stomach felt hot.

explain: 몸의 한 곳이 갑자기 뜨거워지는 느낌을 나타내는 의태어예요. 부끄러울 때 '얼굴이 화끈거리다', 매운 걸 먹은 뒤 '입이 화끈거리다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '후끈'은 공기나 방이 갑자기 더워지는 느낌에 더 어울려요.
explain_en: An onomatopoeic adverb for a part of the body suddenly feeling hot. Used as '얼굴이 화끈거리다' when embarrassed or '입이 화끈거리다' after eating spicy food. The similar '후끈' fits air or a room suddenly turning warm.
